issues.title: select --verify reports successful label-based selections as failures (and never affects the exit code)

sections.body:
On a page with <select> options whose value differs from the visible label (e.g. the form-filling fixture: value 'sg', label 'Singapore'):
1. browser4-cli select e1918 "Singapore" --verify
   → prints "✓ Selected 'Singapore' in e1918" then "Verification: expected 'Singapore' to be selected, but current value is 'sg'." (exit code 0).
2. browser4-cli select e1918 "sg" --verify
   → prints "Verification: option 'sg' is selected." (same selection, both exit 0).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: When the option was successfully selected by its visible label, --verify should confirm success (resolve label → option value, case-insensitively) instead of printing a failure message. A genuine verification failure should produce a non-zero exit code so scripts can rely on it.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: select accepts both the option label and the option value as <val> and selects correctly in both cases, but --verify compares the raw argument string (exact, case-sensitive) against element.value, so any label-based or case-differing selection prints a misleading 'expected … but current value is …' failure line. All verification branches return Ok, so exit code is 0 whether verification passed or failed.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: verify_select_result in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:8828 reads element.value via browser_evaluate and compares it with expected_value using exact equality (main.rs:8852). The select tool itself matches option text OR value server-side, so the verify step's value-only, case-sensitive comparison disagrees with the select semantics. Verification outcome is printed via Ok(...) in every branch (main.rs:8852-8864), never Err, so exit code cannot signal failure.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:verify_select_result (line 8828)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Make --verify resolve the expected label to its option value before comparing (e.g. evaluate the option list and match label case-insensitively, or compare against both option.text and option.value).
- Normalize case on comparison so 'Advanced' vs 'advanced' does not fail.
- Return Err (non-zero exit) when verification genuinely fails; treat label/value/case matches as success.
- Keep the success/failure wording consistent with the select argument actually accepted ('option "Singapore" (value sg) is selected').
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: select help text does not document that <val> accepts label or value, nor what --verify compares

sections.body: browser4-cli help select → shows only '<val>  Value to select in the dropdown' and a bare '--verify  Verify the correct option was selected by reading the element value'. No mention that the visible option text (e.g. 'Singapore') or the option value ('sg') are both accepted, that matching is case-insensitive on labels, or that --verify compares against element.value only.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Help should state: <val> may be the option's visible label or its value; --verify compares the argument against the select's value attribute, so passing a label with differing value triggers a mismatch message (see the verify issue).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A first-time user has no way to know the accepted input forms; the only in-session signal is the confusing --verify message discovered by accident.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Command help definitions in commands.rs describe select minimally; SKILL.md lists select under interaction commands with no worked example (unlike fill/click which have several). No reference doc exists for select at all.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (select command help definition, near the 'no-snapshot' OptionDef at line 1005); skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md §6 Quick Patterns
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Extend the select help text: '<val> Option value or visible label to select'.
- Document --verify comparison semantics and note it is advisory (exit code unaffected) until the verify bug is fixed.
- Add a one-line select example to SKILL.md Quick Patterns next to the form-fill example.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Non-browser commands missing from the no-snapshot allowlist trigger a full page snapshot (config list prints '### Page' and writes a YAML snapshot file)

sections.body: With an active browser session: browser4-cli config list → prints the four config values, then also '### Page / Page URL / Page Title / ### Snapshot / [Snapshot](...\.browser4-cli\snapshot\snapshot-....yml)' and a tip line, and writes a new snapshot file to disk. Verified twice (two snapshot files created purely by config list invocations).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: config list is a local read-only CLI command; it should print configuration only and should not capture a browser accessibility snapshot, add ~1-3s latency, or write files.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Any command not in the no_snapshot_commands() allowlist triggers post_command_snapshot() whenever a session is active (main.rs:18438). 'config' is absent from the allowlist, so config list behaves like an interaction command. Output clutter plus snapshot-disk accumulation on every invocation (100+ YAML files now present in .browser4-cli/snapshot, mostly from interactions in previous sessions).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: main.rs:18433-18443 implements an opt-out allowlist (no_snapshot_commands(), main.rs:362) that enumerates commands that skip the auto-snapshot. Non-browser/management commands such as 'config' were never added to the list; the allowlist design means any new command silently inherits browser-snapshot behavior. The comment at main.rs:18431 ('commands that modify browser state') does not match the implementation.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:no_snapshot_commands() (line 362) and post-command snapshot call site (line 18438); post_command_snapshot at line 1041
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add 'config' (and audit 'plugin', 'skills', 'experience', 'webminer', 'swarm', 'crawl' subcommand families) to no_snapshot_commands().
- Invert the design: only run the post-command snapshot for a small explicit set of interaction commands (fill/click/type/press/select/check/…) rather than for everything except an allowlist.
- Add a regression unit test asserting config-style commands do not trigger post-command snapshots.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: ★ marker on help rows has no legend in the help output

sections.body: browser4-cli help → many rows are prefixed '★' (goto, snapshot, eval, fill, click, …) with no legend explaining the marker anywhere in the output (grepped the full help text: no '★ =' legend).
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either a legend ('★ = commonly used / high-frequency command') at the top of the Commands section, or removal of the unexplained marker.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: First-time users cannot tell whether ★ denotes importance, a prerequisite, or a category; the meaning exists only in code comments (help.rs:2663 'Mark high-frequency commands with a ★ so first-time users can …') and in an unrelated selector-quality legend elsewhere in the codebase.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: help.rs:2663 marks high-frequency commands in category listings but the rendered help table never defines the symbol. Minor, but the marker is aimed precisely at first-time users, the group least able to guess its meaning.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs:2663 (category-listing renderer that emits the marker)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Print a legend line after the Commands heading: '★ = high-frequency command — good starting points for new users'.
- Alternatively drop the marker from category listings and rely on the Quick Start box already present.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: snapshot -v 0 captures a mid-page chunk after interactions that auto-scroll; no actionable hint that the page top is above the current viewport

sections.body: After filling the form and clicking the submit button (which sits at y≈1573, below the 1080px viewport, so the driver scrolls it into view), run: browser4-cli snapshot -v 0 --stdout. The output header shows '# hiddenTopHeight: 1057px' but the tree starts mid-page: the top-of-page confirmation text ('Submission Result / Your form data was captured successfully.', at y≈434-747) is excluded from the capture because it lies above the visible band.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The captured 'result page' chunk should be recognizable as not starting at the page top, and the help/docs should tell the user how to reach the top chunk (-v -1, or scroll up first) when they intend to document the page from the top.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The doc table says '-v 0 = current visible screen' and the header comment lists hiddenTopHeight, so the behavior technically matches the docs — but a first-time user reading '-v 0' as 'top of the result page' silently produces an artifact missing the confirmation heading. SKILL.md only clarifies the scroll-relative semantics for fresh navigations ('After a fresh navigation -v 0 is the top of the page'); this page did not navigate on submit.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Click interactions that target below-the-fold elements scroll the page; viewport indices are scroll-relative, so -v 0 no longer equals the page top after such a click. The snapshot footer comment (viewports/scroll hints) does not warn when hiddenTopHeight is large.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (snapshot output footer generation / viewport hint); skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md §5 snapshot-modes table
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- When hiddenTopHeight > 0, print an actionable hint with the snapshot (e.g. '# Note: page is scrolled 1057px down; use snapshot -v -1 or scroll up to capture the page top').
- Extend the SKILL.md snapshot-modes row: '-v 0 = current visible screen; after clicks that auto-scroll elements into view this may be mid-page — use -v -1/-v 0 after scrolling to top for the page start'.
- Consider a 'snapshot --top' convenience flag that scrolls to top (or maps to viewport 0 of a fresh scroll) before capturing.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
